source_name: Saudi Vision 2030 -- Non-Oil GDP Gap Tracker
rationale: Vision 2030's own tracker states non-oil GDP is running at roughly 55% of total GDP in 2025 against a 65% target. This is a third-party analytics/tracker site rather than a primary GASTAT or IMF publication, and a corroborating primary IMF/World Bank figure for the identical year could not be located, so kept at Medium confidence.

source_name: UAE Federal Competitiveness and Statistics Centre (FCSC) 2024 GDP data, reported by Khaleej Times
rationale: FCSC (UAE's national statistics agency) reported non-oil activities at 75.5% of total 2024 GDP. Corroborated independently by Gulf News, Gulf Business, and AGBI reporting the same FCSC release.

source_name: Qatar National Planning Council (NPC) statistics release
rationale: Qatar's national statistics body reported non-hydrocarbon activities at nearly 64% of total 2024 GDP. Consistent with IMF's 2024 Article IV characterization of Qatar's nonhydrocarbon economy as 'about two-thirds' of output.

source_name: Bahrain Ministry of Finance and National Economy -- Bahrain Economic Report 2024
rationale: Bahrain's Ministry of Finance states non-oil activities contributed 86.0% to real GDP in 2024. Reported consistently across Arab News and Economy Middle East coverage of the same official release.

source_name: AGBI -- Kuwait's 2024 GDP falls $5bn due to oil price drop (citing Kuwait national accounts data)
rationale: Kuwait's 2024 national accounts show the oil sector at ~43% of GDP against non-oil GDP of ~57%. A national-accounts oil-sector share relayed via financial press rather than a primary government release, and computed (100 minus oil share) rather than a directly stated figure -- Medium confidence.

source_name: Oman Ministry of Finance, citing National Centre for Statistics and Information (NCSI) preliminary 2024 data
rationale: Oman's Ministry of Finance states oil and gas activities reached 29.0% of GDP in 2024, implying non-oil activities at approximately 71%. Corroborated by NCSI underlying value figures reported by Oman Observer and Muscat Daily.

Pakistan is not a hydrocarbon-rent economy -- a net oil/gas importer with domestic hydrocarbon production a negligible share of GDP -- so a non-oil GDP share proxy does not meaningfully apply. Structural non-applicability, not a data gap.
Turkey is a diversified, manufacturing- and services-led economy with minimal domestic oil production and no meaningful oil-rent share of GDP, so this proxy is not a meaningful lens for it.
Israel is a diversified, technology- and services-led economy with essentially no oil rents, so a non-oil GDP share framing is not a meaningful or commonly published metric for it.

source_name: World Bank -- Oil rents (% of GDP), Egypt, Arab Rep. (indicator NY.GDP.PETR.RT.ZS)
rationale: World Bank data puts Egypt's oil rents at only ~2.99% of GDP in 2021, confirming Egypt is not a hydrocarbon-rent economy in the sense this proxy is designed for; a '100 minus oil rents' computation would misleadingly imply ~97% 'non-oil' diversification on par with a rentier state. Treated as not applicable rather than forcing a misleading number.
Jordan has no significant domestic oil production and negligible oil rents as a share of GDP, so this proxy is not a meaningful metric for its economy.

source_name: World Bank -- Iraq Macro Poverty Outlook (MPO), April 2025 update
rationale: World Bank's Iraq MPO states oil accounted for an estimated 53% of real GDP in 2025, implying a non-oil share of roughly 47%. Other sources give somewhat different contemporaneous estimates (differing real vs nominal GDP methodologies) -- flagged as approximate, hence Medium confidence.
Lebanon has no commercial oil or gas production and no oil-rent revenue base, so this proxy is not meaningful for an economy instead defined by its 2019-onward banking/currency collapse.

Syria's pre-war oil sector was already a modest GDP share, and post-2011 conflict/sanctions have effectively collapsed formal oil-rent GDP accounting; no reliable current breakdown exists, so marked not applicable rather than estimated.

source_name: World Bank -- Oil rents (% of GDP), Iran, Islamic Rep. (indicator NY.GDP.PETR.RT.ZS)
rationale: World Bank data puts Iran's oil rents at 18.27% of GDP in 2021, the most recent year with a publicly reported figure, implying a non-oil proxy of ~81.7%. The IMF has not conducted a published Article IV consultation with Iran since 2018; this figure is dated (2021) and relayed via secondary reporting rather than confirmed directly against the primary database, hence Low confidence.

Yemen's oil production has been severely disrupted by ongoing conflict and blockades since 2022, collapsing what was already a modest oil-rent GDP share; no reliable current breakdown exists, so marked not applicable rather than estimated.
Afghanistan has no meaningful domestic oil production or oil-rent revenue base at any point in its recent economic history, so this proxy is not a meaningful or ever-published metric for its economy.
